title: Pascal's Triangle
statement:
Pascal's triangle is built row by row. Row 0 is just `1`. Every other row has one more entry than the row above it: its first and last entries are `1`, and every entry in between is the sum of the two entries directly above it in the previous row.

Given `numRows`, print the first `numRows` rows of the triangle (rows `0` to `numRows - 1`).
outputFormat: Print `numRows` lines. Line `i` (starting from 0) contains the `i + 1` entries of row `i`, separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: The last row is built from 1 4 6 4 1: 1, 1+4, 4+6, 6+4, 4+1, 1.

hints: Each row depends only on the row directly above it, so build the rows in order.
Row i has i + 1 entries; the first and last are 1.
For 0 < j < i, row[i][j] = row[i-1][j-1] + row[i-1][j].
